questions.questionText: A collection of operations that form a single logical unit of work.
The equivalent of single SQL statement in an application program or transaction.
A state that satisfies the constraints specified the schema.
A record that keeps track of all transactions that update the database.
4 properties of transaction.
To maintain the integrity of a database, all transactions must obey ACID properties.
Requires that all operations (SQL requests) should be completed.
It ensures that only valid data following all rules and constraints will be written in the database.
Means that the data used during the execution of a current transaction cannot be used by another transaction.
Ensures that data once transaction changes are done and committed, they cannot be undone or lost.
This marks the beginning of transaction execution.
This signals a successful end of the transaction.

questions.questionText: It is needed when several transactions execute simultaneously in the database.
Occurs when transaction 1 and 2 are updating the same data element and one of the updates are lost.
Occurs when two transactions. T1 and T2, are executed currently, and the first transaction (T1) is rolled back after the second transaction (T2) has already accessed the uncommitted data.
Occur when a transaction accesses data before and after one or more other transactions finish working with the same data.
It guarantees exclusive use of data item that is currently used by transaction T1.
Prevents access to any row by transaction T2 while transaction T1 is using the table.
Allows concurrent transactions to access different rows of the same table even when the rows are located on the same page.
Prevents access to any row by transaction while transaction is using the table.
Has only two states: locked or unlocked. If an object such as a database, table, or row is locked by a transaction, no other transaction can use that object.

This lock exists when access is reserved specifically for the transaction that locked the object. This other lock exists when a transaction wants to read data from the database, and no exclusive lock has held that data item.
It occurs when two transactions wait indefinitely for each other to unlock data.
A transaction requesting a new lock is aborted when there is the possibility that a deadlock can occur.
The DBMS periodically tests the database for deadlocks.
The transaction must obtain all the locks it needs before it can be executed.
Issues may occur when many people/users read and write the same data. This common issue can be identified as Read Phenomena.
Transaction levels are described by the type of '_____' that a transaction allows or not.
A transaction can read data that is not committed yet.
A transaction reads a data twice and yields a different result from each read is a non-repeatable read. The original data may have been updated or deleted by another transaction.
A transaction executes a query at a time, and when then it runs the same query at the time, yielding additional rows that satisfy the query.
Can read modified data values that have not yet been committed by other transactions; these are called 'dirty reads'.
Prevents dirty reads by specifying that statements cannot read data values that have been modified but not yet been committed by other transactions.
Ensures that no other transaction can modify or delete data has been read by the current transactions until the current transaction commits.
Ensures that the data that one transaction has read, will be prevented from being updated or delete by any other transaction.
